restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 (C=2140): CF31 is issued on register-resident padded-block and IV words; one issue costs 1 unit plus one ordinary op; every other primitive word operation costs 1/2140.
Complete fixed-IV SHA-256, steps 0..30 with full feed-forward, FIPS 180-4 padding, all 256 output bits; 32-byte single-block messages msg(x)=BE32(x).

Generic van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point search on one processor: theta=2^-32, L=2^40, K0=65162*2^112, Dcap=2^98, BLOCK unrolled 16 ways with a DP test after every evaluation, one run and no restart.

Calling convention: CF31 reads W[0..15] from R0..R15 and IV from R16..R23; writes the digest H[0..7] into R0..R7 only; may clobber R8..R15; does not write R16..R23. Padding is rewritten each evaluation; IV is written once in setup.
Time, memory and preprocessing are worst-case for every run. Success probability >=0.39 depends only on score-critical heuristic H-RF (analytic lower bound 0.3900080).
Generic construction; no stored collision, nonuniform advice, or claimed cryptanalytic improvement.

heuristics.statement: Random-function model for f(x)=SHA-256-r31(BE32(x)): an evaluation of f at a point not previously evaluated returns a value uniform on {0,1}^256 and independent of the algorithm's coins and of all values observed so far. Used only to lower-bound success probability. Output correctness and all resource bounds are unconditional.
heuristics.scope: The fixed 31-step SHA-256 map on 32-byte messages along the charged van Oorschot-Wiener chains of this package (theta=2^-32, L=2^40, K0=65162*2^112, Dcap=2^98), covering at most K0-1+L main-loop evaluations and at most 2^98+2^88+2 chains.
heuristics.extrapolation: Standard generic modelling of a fixed cryptographic compression as a random function on the walk points, consistent with peer exploratory DP packages on this track. Supporting reduced-output measurements (n=24..48) are documented in the proof as non-organizer evidence and do not enter the analytic bound.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is a heuristic, not a theorem about a fixed deterministic function. Published differential attacks on 31-step SHA-256 exhibit structure on chosen pairs; this walk does not select such pairs. Reduced-width experiments cannot exclude a full-width deviation. The analytic margin above 0.39 is only about 8e-6; a small overestimate of contact probability would require a slightly larger K0.
